app_info.descriptions: A polyglot Slack clone: nine TypeScript roles (svc-auth, svc-workspace, svc-channel, svc-message, svc-thread, svc-file, svc-search, svc-notification, svc-platform) behind an Envoy edge, Go real-time and connection services (ws-gateway, flannel, channel-rt, dispatcher, kafkagate, search-engine), Python async workers over Redpanda, and PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO for state. Every application role exposes GET/PUT /admin/config, POST /admin/reload, GET/PUT /admin/event and /admin/sequencer on port 8000; the database maintenance controller exposes /v1/maintenance on db-maintenance:8081. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

Every application role exposes GET/PUT /admin/config, POST /admin/reload, GET/PUT /admin/event and /admin/sequencer on port 8000; the database maintenance controller exposes /v1/maintenance on db-maintenance:8081. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

app_info.descriptions:
Frappe Framework (the platform under ERPNext) serving a single site through gunicorn/nginx Desk APIs, with MariaDB for data, a Redis cache, and a Redis queue (RQ) drained by a long-queue background worker. Background work includes emails, prepared report exports and scheduled jobs. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: mysql with the MariaDB root DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, python3, and reconfigure-infra.sh for bounded Redis queue repairs (it applies them through the frappe-admin service so they survive a broker restart). MariaDB and Redis exporters are scraped by Prometheus.

An incident ticket has been filed for this deployment:

> Busy periods are knocking users out of Desk. Pages that worked a moment earlier return errors until traffic settles, then browsing, search, and dashboards recover. Background work is broken even during quiet hours: queued emails and report exports never arrive, and scheduled jobs do not run.
>
> These are separate failures, so do not stop after fixing one of them. Make sure both problems are resolved.
>
> Preserve queued work and keep the queue's finite, loss-intolerant memory policy through a broker restart. Flushing data, changing the cache tier, worker scaling, traffic suppression, or restart-only recovery is not acceptable.

Ground rules from the incident runbook: repair the live system in place through its operational surfaces (database administration, broker configuration, the toolbox helpers). Preserve queued work. Broad grants, flushing data, cache-style eviction, scaling workers, suppressing traffic, and restart-only workarounds are not acceptable.

Every application role exposes GET/PUT /admin/config, POST /admin/reload, GET/PUT /admin/event and /admin/sequencer on port 8000; the database maintenance controller exposes /v1/maintenance on db-maintenance:8081. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

app_info.descriptions: A polyglot Slack clone: nine TypeScript roles (svc-auth, svc-workspace, svc-channel, svc-message, svc-thread, svc-file, svc-search, svc-notification, svc-platform) behind an Envoy edge, Go real-time and connection services (ws-gateway, flannel, channel-rt, dispatcher, kafkagate, search-engine), Python async workers over Redpanda, and PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO for state. Every application role exposes GET/PUT /admin/config, POST /admin/reload, GET/PUT /admin/event and /admin/sequencer on port 8000; the database maintenance controller exposes /v1/maintenance on db-maintenance:8081. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

app_info.descriptions: A polyglot Slack clone: nine TypeScript roles (svc-auth, svc-workspace, svc-channel, svc-message, svc-thread, svc-file, svc-search, svc-notification, svc-platform) behind an Envoy edge, Go real-time and connection services (ws-gateway, flannel, channel-rt, dispatcher, kafkagate, search-engine), Python async workers over Redpanda, and PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO for state. Every application role exposes GET/PUT /admin/config, POST /admin/reload, GET/PUT /admin/event and /admin/sequencer on port 8000; the database maintenance controller exposes /v1/maintenance on db-maintenance:8081. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

app_info.descriptions:
Saleor headless e-commerce (Django/GraphQL API under uvicorn plus a Celery worker) over PostgreSQL, Valkey and RabbitMQ, driven by cyclical storefront traffic (browsing and checkouts). Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged PostgreSQL DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl for the GraphQL API at $SALEOR_API_URL, and RabbitMQ management credentials in $RABBITMQ_ADMIN_URL. PostgreSQL, Valkey and RabbitMQ exporters are scraped by Prometheus.

An incident ticket has been filed for this deployment:

> Checkout failures line up with storefront traffic spikes, but they’re intermittent. Between bursts, the Saleor API looks healthy. That’s made the cause hard to catch.
>
> Find the underlying cause and fix it without broad changes. We cannot restart Saleor or PostgreSQL during this incident, so the repair needs to work in place. Keep existing orders and the rest of the platform intact.
>
> Before handing this back, make sure checkouts stay healthy through another busy period and across new database sessions.

Ground rules from the incident runbook: repair the live system in place through its operational surfaces (database administration, the application's own APIs). Restarting or redeploying workloads, broad configuration changes, and anything that drops data or suppresses traffic are not acceptable.

app_info.descriptions:
A polyglot Slack clone: nine TypeScript roles (svc-auth, svc-workspace, svc-channel, svc-message, svc-thread, svc-file, svc-search, svc-notification, svc-platform) behind an Envoy edge, Go real-time and connection services (ws-gateway, flannel, channel-rt, dispatcher, kafkagate, search-engine), Python async workers over Redpanda, and PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO for state. Every application role exposes GET/PUT /admin/config, POST /admin/reload, GET/PUT /admin/event and /admin/sequencer on port 8000; the database maintenance controller exposes /v1/maintenance on db-maintenance:8081. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

An incident ticket has been filed for this deployment:

> The message delivery path has been flaky even though traffic looks normal. Figure out what is actually causing it and fix the problem without broad or unrelated changes. Make sure it stays gone after one restart and remains stable while traffic continues.

Ground rules from the incident runbook: repair the live system in place through its operational surfaces (each service's /admin API, the maintenance API, database administration, service configuration). The deployed application release is approved and must stay as it is. Restarting or rescaling workloads to mask a problem, raising capacity limits beyond the peer roles' budget, disabling safeguards or routine maintenance, and suppressing traffic are not acceptable.

app_info.descriptions: An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services. Customers report cart items disappearing or reappearing between visits after a release cutover. Restore consistent carts while preserving every acknowledged add and clear, including earlier customer state. Example sessions are in ConfigMap customer-support; normal application logs and traces retain customer activity. Availability alone is insufficient. Maintenance may pause cart traffic by setting acceptWrites=false in ConfigMap storefront-operations; wait for status=paused before reconciling data, then resume service. Preserve at least two serving frontend-proxy replicas. Unacknowledged requests, if any, are listed by trace ID in that operational record. The frontend-retained and cart-retained Service entrypoints are scheduled for retirement. Public cart operations must remain correct when those entrypoints are withdrawn and callers are replaced. Either database may remain authoritative; do not discard acknowledged customer state.

An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

app_info.descriptions: A polyglot Slack clone: nine TypeScript roles (svc-auth, svc-workspace, svc-channel, svc-message, svc-thread, svc-file, svc-search, svc-notification, svc-platform) behind an Envoy edge, Go real-time and connection services (ws-gateway, flannel, channel-rt, dispatcher, kafkagate, search-engine), Python async workers over Redpanda, and PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO for state. Every application role exposes GET/PUT /admin/config, POST /admin/reload, GET/PUT /admin/event and /admin/sequencer on port 8000; the database maintenance controller exposes /v1/maintenance on db-maintenance:8081. Ported from Incident Arena. An `ops-toolbox` pod provides an operator shell: psql with the privileged DSN in $DB_ADMIN_DSN, curl, and restart-svc.sh (applies a JSON config block to a role through PUT /admin/config + POST /admin/reload). Application and PostgreSQL metrics are scraped by Prometheus.
